title: Own each duplicated fragment once within its layer

facts.note: Only TypeScript source files are compared.
Tests, specs, .d.ts, index.ts barrels and __tests__ directories are excluded.
Both files must resolve to the SAME architectural layer; unclassified paths are never judged.

Requires the bun_ts_metrics_detector cross-file fingerprint scan over the whole tree. It applies to every qualifying same-layer pair, whether newly introduced or pre-existing (strict, no baseline); it is not gated on which files the current diff touched.

fires: A run of 7+ non-trivial normalized lines in one domain-layer file also appears in another domain-layer file, even if variables were renamed and literals differ.
Two application-layer handlers share a run of 7+ non-trivial normalized executable lines differing only in identifiers and string literals.
A qualifying same-layer duplicate already existed before the current task and is untouched by the diff; the whole-tree scan still reports it.
doesNotFire: The same shape appears once in the domain layer and once in the presentation layer.
The match is in test/spec files, .d.ts files, index.ts barrels or __tests__ directories.
The only matching lines are import/re-export declarations, bare braces/closing punctuation, or property signatures of type/interface bodies.
One or both files cannot be assigned to a layer.
The duplicated run is shorter than 7 non-trivial normalized lines.

given: two non-test TypeScript files in the same layer share a run of 7+ non-trivial lines that match after normalization (comments stripped; identifiers, strings and numbers folded, so renames don't hide it)
when: the whole-tree duplication scan reports the pair (DUPLICATION-TS-001), new or pre-existing
then: Resolve it semantically: own one shared concept once within that layer, or make the real differences of two distinct responsibilities explicit.
prefer: Before extracting, check both share a responsibility and change reason, find the smallest stable shared behavior, and confirm it belongs in that layer.
For one concept, extract a focused function/module within the layer.
Name shared behavior by its domain or responsibility.
For different responsibilities, keep them independent and express real differences directly.
avoid: Renaming identifiers, changing literals, reordering harmless statements or other cosmetic edits to defeat normalization.
Cross-layer abstractions made just because layers hold similar-shaped code.
Highly parameterized generic helpers that obscure callers' intent.
Forcing distinct responsibilities into one abstraction to remove the finding.
A refactor that removes this finding but introduces new ATDD Bun violations.
unless: Tests, specs, .d.ts, index.ts barrels and __tests__ dirs are excluded.
Files with no determinable layer are not judged.
why: A duplicate fingerprint is only a sensor that two sites MAY share one responsibility or change reason, so diagnose before extracting. The intra-layer limit is deliberate: twice in one layer is the shape that genuinely wants extracting; across layers it is usually two obligations, and merging couples layers that should move independently.
evidence: The DUPLICATION-TS-001 finding for the pair is gone after the change.
The duplicate was removed because ownership became clearer or because genuine semantic differences are now explicit — not via renames, literal changes or reordering.
Dependency direction and layer boundaries remain valid (no cross-layer abstraction introduced).
Any extracted abstraction has one coherent reason to change.
Existing behavior and tests remain green.
The refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations (the atdd-bun run after the change reports no new findings).
verifier_detail: Threshold: a run of 7 or more non-trivial normalized lines appearing in two different TypeScript files of the SAME architectural layer is a finding.

Normalization per line: strip comments, fold string literals to "S", numbers to 0, non-keyword identifiers to ID; so renaming a variable cannot hide a duplicate and the fingerprint tracks STRUCTURE rather than text.

Trivial lines (bare braces, closing punctuation) are dropped and not counted toward the 7; then every sliding window of 7 lines is fingerprinted (sha256-prefix fingerprint) and compared only within a layer.
Import and re-export declarations are not counted: two files importing the same names from one shared module match because the logic was shared, which is the fix this rule asks for.

Property signatures inside a `type X = {` or `interface X {` body (optional `readonly`, a name, optional `?`, `:` a type, ending `;` or `,`), including members of nested object types, are not counted: unrelated records with the same number of same-typed fields match once identifiers are folded, and neither coupling them nor a cosmetic edit is a fix.
Executable statements, object literals, class fields, enum bodies and method bodies still count.

Excluded files: test, spec, `.d.ts`, `index.ts` barrels, `__tests__` directories. Files with undeterminable layer are not judged, because with no established layer there is no intra-layer comparison; unclassified paths are never compared with each other.
Detector: bun_ts_metrics_detector (validator); core alias DUPLICATION-TS-001; severity 2; disposition strict (every finding fails, including pre-existing ones).
